clue.text: Royal sycophant is cooking local delicacy

indicators.note: cooking up something means concocting it, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: R, from Rex or Regina, is the standard abbreviation for royal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fawning courtier is busy in the kitchen preparing a regional speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' shuffles R plus SYCOPHANTIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This crimped pie of meat and vegetables is the traditional regional food of Cornwall, in south-west England.

clue.text: Women breaking crockery good for gossip

indicators.note: the women break into the crockery, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: china is fine crockery

explanation.surface: Women smash plates, which turns out well for those who like a bit of tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat or natter is informal talk, the same idle chatter as gossip in its noun sense.

clue.text: Comic actor is concerning First Lady

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
Eve was the first woman, in Genesis

explanation.surface: A funny performer is involved with the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a President's spouse, but it is Eve. The actor is Christopher Reeve, who played Superman, the hero of the comics.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Reeve starred as Superman, a comic-book hero, making him an actor known from comics.

clue.text: Disdain for man trying to smuggle grass

indicators.note: the clue words carry the answer secretly inside them, as smuggled goods are carried

explanation.surface: Someone looks down on a man who tries to sneak cannabis through customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the drug being smuggled, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is someone who tells the police about criminals, a police tip-off source.

clue.text: Rings Tramp

parts.note: a hob is a cooker top, made up of cooking rings
the letter O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Telephones a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Rings' does both jobs: a hob is a set of cooking rings, and O is a single ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An American word for a homeless wanderer or vagrant, a down-and-out drifter.

clue.text: Two continents like supporting destruction of Crimea

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after
the place name is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: anagram fodder
as means like, in the sense of similar to

explanation.surface: Two continents back the destruction of the Black Sea peninsula, a geopolitical headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destruction of' rearranges CRIMEA into AMERIC; 'supporting' puts AS below it.
explanation.definitionFit: North and South America are together often called the Americas, a plural name for that pair of landmasses.

clue.text: Entice politician to visit street regularly

indicators.note: the politician goes into the letters, as a visitor goes into a house
taking every other letter of the word street leaves an evenly spaced selection

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A lawmaker is lured into making the rounds of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every second letter of 'street'; 'to visit' puts the politician inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone is to tempt them, a straight synonym for attracting with promise.

clue.text: Gets a tan at sea, being idle

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathes on a cruise, lazing about with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges GETSATAN. 'idle' is a verb here: to do nothing, to vegetate.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to be inactive, and to stagnate is likewise to stay still and make no progress.

clue.text: Uncaring bastard set fire to what on return?

parts.note: B is the polite shorthand for the swear word, as in 'the b-'
lit means set fire to, as a match lit a candle

indicators.note: a word coming back is read from right to left

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: An outraged question about some heartless brute who committed arson.
explanation.walkthrough: B for 'bastard' is the coy written stand-in for the swear word, as in 'the b-'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carefree or casually indifferent fits uncaring, a near synonym for unconcerned.

clue.text: Healthy cycling myth is beyond words

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from the front to the back

parts.note: fine means well or healthy
a fable is a myth or legend

explanation.surface: The legend that cycling is good for you is too wonderful to put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves F from the front of FINE to the back, making INEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great or extreme to be expressed in language is indescribable, beyond words.

clue.text: Mark and others lead as one

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, a former German currency
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Mark and his companions take charge together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb meaning guide, but it is the element Pb, and 'as one' says it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy element of the kind called metallic, one example of the class.

clue.text: Vessel with drink that has no head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: sherry is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A boat comes with a drink missing its froth.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge, a kind of vessel on rivers.

clue.text: Look drunk, beyond question

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone's inebriated appearance is undeniable.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument with no holes in it is watertight, figuratively unassailable and beyond question.

clue.text: Leave Indian coastal path?

parts.note: Goa is a coastal state of western India
a way is a path

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a seaside walking route in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' is an imperative here, an order to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Leave!' as a command means be off, a curt order for someone to depart.

clue.text: Clear Italian drink Greek is wanting opening

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the Greek letters are taken away

parts.note: grappa is an Italian brandy made from grape residue
a rent is a tear or gap, an opening

explanation.surface: A clear Italian spirit, while a Greek wants an aperitif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wanting' removes GR from GRAPPA, leaving APPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see or obvious is clear, and the adjective here means evident.

clue.text: Tackle difficult conflict with European

parts.note: hard means difficult
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Taking on a hard fight with someone from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb but is the noun: gear or equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle as a noun means equipment or gear, and tools and fittings are called hardware.

clue.text: Chapter I'd rewritten for next to nothing

indicators.note: writing again lets the letters be set down in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An author would redo a chapter for a pittance.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying something for next to nothing means buying it extremely cheaply, at a bargain price.

clue.text: Prostitute's position when US President enters

indicators.note: the President goes in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: set can mean position, as in to set something down
Donald Trump is a US President

explanation.surface: A seedy political scandal: a sex worker's place when the President walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prostitute's' reads as possessive but is the definition followed by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned, derogatory term for a woman who sells sex, synonymous with harlot.

clue.text: Maybe disarm a friend's hiding place

indicators.note: the friend hides the place, holding it concealed inside

parts.note: a mate is a friend
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A buddy's secret hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe disarm' is a definition by example: to disarm can literally mean to cut off an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off a limb surgically is to cut it away; disarm, read literally, is one example.

clue.text: Not totally relaxed, compere going completely topless

indicators.note: each word loses its top, its first letter, all of them

parts.note: calm means relaxed
a host is a compere or presenter

explanation.surface: A laid-back TV presenter nearly strips off completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going completely topless' removes the first letters of both CALM and HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly but not totally, falling just short, is an adverb for very close to complete.

clue.text: Stray fibres in underwear

indicators.note: stray letters wander out of place, and are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Loose threads caught in one's pants.
explanation.definitionFit: Short close-fitting knickers or underpants are called briefs, a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Like two peas in a pod? Nearly — essentially comparable

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the phrase after 'like' is a stock simile, a comparison using like or as
the last letter, the one 'Nearly' leaves off

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its central letters

parts.note: near-identical, alike in their essentials

explanation.surface: Musing that two things are as alike as peas in a pod, or nearly, essentially comparable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as part of the stock phrase, but it is the definition; the phrase that follows is an example of a figure of speech. 'Nearly' cuts the E from SIMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Like as an adjective means resembling or alike, as in things of like kind.

clue.text: Egg-based treat provided by farmer in Guernsey

indicators.note: the words supply the answer from within themselves, carried across their joins

explanation.surface: A Channel Island farmer supplies a sweet made from his hens' eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: GUERNSEY is a Channel Island known for dairy cattle, which helps the farming surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped egg white baked with sugar makes this crisp sweet, a dessert built from eggs.

clue.text: Corner relative when drunk?

indicators.note: slurred speech turns the s sound into sh, so the word is heard said thickly

parts.note: a niece is a relative

explanation.surface: A tipsy relative skulking in the corner of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' says the word is slurred, so a kinswoman's word comes out as 'neesh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess or nook in a wall is a corner, small hollow space.

clue.text: 13 taking ecstasy for a laugh

indicators.note: taking in means holding something inside

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a curt order to leave, gives the slang word scram
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: an order to depart taking drugs for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts E inside SCRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is called a scream, informally a laugh, an amusing thing or person.

clue.text: She used to serve porridge once, prepared around ten

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
prepared means made ready, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: anagram fodder
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A dinner lady used to dish up oats, prepared round about ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges ONCE into ECON, which goes 'around' X. In British slang, porridge is time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who once served time in prison is a former convict, a release from jail.

clue.text: Jeer Republican oaf

parts.note: to boo is to jeer

explanation.surface: A Republican lout is heckled.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish lout is a rude, clumsy person, a synonym for an oaf.

clue.text: Lad in charge of sound

parts.note: a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy put in charge of the audio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective for acoustic matters, relating to sound waves.

clue.text: Language in France established by craftsmen and labourers, originally

parts.note: proven means established as true

indicators.note: originally points to the origins, the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: A French tongue was founded by the work of artisans and workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occitan dialect of Provence in southern France is a regional tongue spoken there.

clue.text: Dear for one to provide paper knife?

definitions.meaning: the salutation Dear is how correspondence typically begins

explanation.surface: A cherished one gives a knife for paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear starts a letter, and the term also names the blade used to slit envelopes.
